description: Which option answers an ACP permission request (session/request_permission) when the user approves or denies it: among the options whose kind contains allow (or reject), the first whose kind contains once, else the first; none answers the request cancelled. So a controller press never silently grants or denies "always". Kinds are matched with Swift's String.contains, whole clusters, case-sensitively.
function: ACPAdapter.permissionChoice(options:allow:) ↔ powerup_core::harness::acp::permission::permission_choice — input {options: [{optionId, kind}], allow}; expected the chosen optionId, or null (answered cancelled)
capturedAgainst: ACPAdapter.swift's permissionChoice as of dddf9c6 (Swift 5.9.2, macOS 27.2)

cases.name: allow picks allow_once over allow_always
cases.reason: HK-131: a controller press must never silently grant "always", so the once variant of the direction wins wherever it is.

cases.name: without a once variant the first allow is picked
cases.reason: HK-131: with no once option the first option of the direction answers.

cases.name: no option of the direction answers nothing
cases.reason: HK-131: no match answers the request cancelled, never the other direction.

cases.name: no options answer nothing
cases.reason: HK-131: an empty option list answers cancelled.

cases.name: disallow counts as an allow kind
cases.reason: HK-131: the kinds are matched with String.contains, so disallow contains allow (kept from Swift).

cases.name: an empty kind matches nothing
cases.reason: HK-131: an option without a kind is neither allow nor reject.

cases.name: the other direction's once is ignored
cases.reason: HK-131: once is looked for only among the options of the chosen direction.

cases.name: of two once options the first wins
cases.reason: HK-131: options keep the agent's order.

cases.name: without a once the first match wins
cases.reason: HK-131: options keep the agent's order.

cases.name: a once listed after an always still wins
cases.reason: HK-131: the once variant is preferred over the first match.

cases.name: a kind with a combining mark after allow is not allow
cases.reason: HK-063, HK-131: String.contains matches whole clusters, so allow followed by a combining acute is no allow (measured with Swift 5.9.2).

cases.name: kinds are case-sensitive
cases.reason: HK-131: ALLOW_ONCE does not contain allow.

cases.name: allow_always_once counts as once
cases.reason: HK-131: any allow kind that contains once is a once variant.

cases.name: reject matches inside a kind
cases.reason: HK-131: contains, not equality: a kind that merely contains reject is a reject option.
